uncertainties.note: Unattributed first-person reaction to the enemy Overman's mind-reading, addressed to Renton; speaker not settled from neighbours (possibly Eureka via the Nirvash link), left unidentified.

'Kokoro no koe' (heart's voice) is Planetta's mind-reading ability; rendered literally and kept consistent so a later reviewer can retitle it centrally if the orchestrator prefers a different term (e.g. 'inner voice').
Source puns on 'untenn daiya' (operating schedule) vs. 'daiyamondo' (diamond); kept as 'schedule' plus an explicit diamond simile so the pun stays visible in English.

Multi-speaker battle-banter exchange among Kashmir, Cynthia/Queen and Gainer; only rows that name a party directly (7542, 7543, 7545, 7548, 7554) are anchored. Untagged lines translated for meaning only, no speaker asserted.

Post-battle bridge/crew exchange about Tiffa, Renton, Gainer and Barrel; individual speakers are not name-tagged in the corpus beyond the addressed party (color(4) name). Context (7498-7500 Garrod/Tiffa scene, 7604's Nirvash reference) strongly suggests Garrod and Renton, but no name was inserted into any row's visible text.

validation.commands: All angle-bracket command sequences (<op()>, <on()>, <sp(20)>, <ab(n)>, <off()>, <color(4)>/<ce()>, <book(61)>/<endbook()>) verified to match the source in exact order for every row via a throwaway comparison script against a fresh `dialogue_corpus.py slice` read; rows 7584-7608 and a few others have no <ab()>/<off()> in source and none was added.
validation.format: Newline counts verified to match source exactly for every row (checked programmatically). ASCII-only text throughout; straight quotes used for the quoted 'Queen' nickname in 7527/7528.
validation.fit: Full meaning drafted first; every row's visible text (commands stripped) verified <= 110 characters, none needed compression.
validation.glossary: Barrel, Kashmir Valle, Planetta, Overman, Overskill, Gekko, Nadesico, Sara Kodama, Exodus taken from character_names_021.json, encyclopedia_022.json, missions_019.json and terms_028.json; 'mobile weapon' (jisou heiki) and 'base' (kyoten) capture wording matched to work/translation/en/hud_labels.json's 2002190 HUD strings for this same mission.
validation.meaning_review: Independent meaning review against the Japanese source (dialogue_corpus.py slice 7412 80 --context 15) found 2 fixes: 07452 restored the speaker's command register ('bring it down for me', not 'I'll do it myself'), and 07486 restored the suki/aishiteru like-then-love escalation with 07487/07489. All 80 rows verified and set to meaning_reviewed; none left in draft. Translator's 'heart's voice' and 'mobile weapon' term choices and unattributed-speaker calls are confirmed correct per orchestrator ruling; see review_07412.json.
